summary: Cecil County, MD steel tower built 1924 near Principio Furnace; a 1935 plan to move it to Elk Neck is unconfirmed; FFLA lists it gone.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower, presented by the Whitaker Iron Company
facts.status_note: Forest Lookout Association's Maryland list marks it gone; no source read confirms the 1935 move or says what remains
facts.agency: Maryland Department of Forestry (planned supervision of the fire station, per the 1924 newspaper)

staffing.status: towerman Harry M. Hartenstine, of Principio, in his ninth year in 1932; later staffing not in the sources read

events.note: Steel tower erected and ready for service in 1924; the Whitaker Iron Company presented the tower
Tower closed for the season in December 1925; the paper said fall fire losses had been small
Harry M. Hartenstine, of Principio, entering his ninth year as towerman; a November 1932 report said no fires had been reported that season
February 1935 newspaper reports a plan to move the tower to the Elk Neck district and raise it 40 feet to 100 feet; no source read confirms the move

sources.title: Forestry Towers and Forestry Tower Properties: A Resource Document

resolved_conflicts.explanation: An August 1924 newspaper described a fifty-foot tower before erection; the state's report for fiscal 1930 gives 60 feet. The record keeps 60 feet (18.3 m) from the state report.

notes_for_editor: Brief staffing 'unknown' replaced with the 1932 towerman. The 1935 Elk Neck move is only a newspaper plan; no source read says it happened. The DNR 2007 report's Black Hill tower (installation probably late 1940s, Elk Neck State Forest) is not linked to Foy's Hill in any source read, so do not treat it as the same structure. The Cecil County history site returned HTTP 403 and was not used; a search snippet from it was not quoted. Confidence medium: the 1924 build and the gone status are well sourced, the tower's end is not.
